$comment: Single source of truth for every public NOVA URL. tools/deploy-check.mjs gates README.md and
docs/*.md against it (local mode) and proves each entry really answers (live mode).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A Vercel host of the shape
is the URL of ONE deployment, not an alias of the project. It is minted at deploy time,
never moves on its own, and stops resolving the moment that deployment is deleted or expires
(preview retention, 'Remove' in Deployments, deleting and recreating the project). The edge
router then answers 404 DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND before your files — or any rewrite in
vercel.json — ever run. So a link like that must never be written into docs, a README, the
GitHub Website field, or a PWA install URL: it is a bookmark of a wave, not of the shore.
The stable address is the project's PRODUCTION domain (Vercel → Settings → Domains), which is
a domain the router keeps pointed at whatever deployment is currently production. Put THAT in
the entry below. Leave 'vercel' empty until a real production domain is attached: an empty
string is an honest TODO that the harness reports as SKIP; a guessed URL is a lie that will
'retired' records hosts that used to be advertised and must never come back. They may appear
in prose only inside the 'Vercel recovery' section of docs/06-install.md (the section whose
job is explaining the death); anywhere else the local gate turns RED.

production.$durableLabels: first labels (without .vercel.app) that belong to THIS project's Production alias — for when the Vercel project is not spelled like the repo, list them here, e.g. [nova, nova-web]. Anything else shaped like <project>-<random>-<team> is a per-deployment URL and is refused.

retired.https://nova-os-topaz-rho.vercel.app/: Vercel-generated URL of a single deployment; 404 DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND since 2026-09-23. Never re-attached to a deployment — see docs/06-install.md#vercel-recovery
